**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The rule's planner hint (`likelyAbsent: true`) was incorrect: Article 11 does contain a dedicated insurance clause at § 11.6 (paragraphs p0573–p0579), which the table of contents also flags.

What it delivers, binding on each Party (so including Harpoon):
- **General liability** with per-occurrence and aggregate minimums, expressly including Clinical Trial Insurance (limits redacted as `[***]`)
- **Workers' compensation** at statutory limits, plus employer's liability, where the Party has U.S. employees
- **Certificates of insurance on request**, occurrence-form policies with a claims-made tail after termination
- A.M. Best "A-VII" or better insurers, with the other Party as additional insured on the GL policy

No professional (E&O) or cyber/privacy layer appears, but Harpoon is a co-development partner in an option structure — it does not host our systems, process Customer Data, or work on our premises — so those preferred limits are not engaged here and the gap is noted in the rationale rather than flagged. Section 11.6.3 also preserves AbbVie's right to self-insure, which runs in our favour and should not be disturbed.

One item worth confirming commercially rather than by redline: the actual dollar limits in 11.6.1 are redacted, so the GL figures cannot be verified against the USD 1M/2M benchmark from the face of the document.
